components.text:
# Philadelphia benefits example

- Explore three library tax benefits and fictional Philly Cash.
- Use the Preview page to try answers and see the effects in the Results section.
- Go to the Publish page to get a unique URL for this screener and see what it will look like to end users.

components.label: Do you live in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania?
components.description: Shared by all four benefits: one answer can feed several checks.

components.label: Would you like extra cash?
components.description: Only used by fictional Philly Cash. A No answer fails that benefit; leaving this blank means unknown. Custom check questions use the custom. prefix; the DMN input is named wantsExtraCash.

components.label: What is your household’s total yearly income?
components.description: Only used by fictional Philly Cash, whose limit is $40,000. A custom check compares this answer with an incomeLimit parameter set on the benefit, so another benefit could reuse the check with a different limit.

components.text:
## Your home

These questions feed the three library tax benefits. Watch which questions become unnecessary as you answer in Preview.

components.label: Do you own and live in your home?
components.description: Shared by Homestead, OOPA, and SCTF.

components.label: Do you owe delinquent property taxes?
Does your property have a ten-year tax abatement?
components.description: Homestead uses a negative check: No passes, Yes fails.

components.label: Which of these programs are you already enrolled in?
components.description: Choose None of these explicitly if you are not enrolled; leaving this blank means enrollment is unknown. Select a program to see its enrollment check fail and the other programs’ checks pass.

components.text:
## Age and family

SCTF can use your age, your spouse’s age, or whether a late spouse was at least 65. The library compares birth dates with the current date.

components.label: Your date of birth
components.description: Try a date more than 65 years ago, then try a younger age.

components.label: Do you currently have a spouse?
components.description: No explicitly records no spouse. Yes links the spouse’s birth date to you for the library age check.

components.label: Your spouse’s date of birth
components.description: Used only when you have a spouse.

components.label: Was your late spouse at least 65?
components.description: Answer No if this does not apply. Leaving it blank can keep the age result unknown when neither birth date establishes eligibility.

components.text:
## Try a few scenarios

**Explore all four:** Philadelphia resident, wants cash, yearly income of $30,000, owns and occupies home, owes delinquent taxes, no abatement, None of these enrollments, birth date over 65 years ago.

**Only Philly Cash passes:** Philadelphia resident, wants cash, yearly income of $30,000, does not own and occupy a home.

**Over the income limit:** change the yearly income to $50,000 to see Philly Cash fail only its income check.

**Unknown cash result:** Philadelphia resident with the extra-cash or income question unanswered.

Philly Cash passes in the first scenario. With None of these, each tax benefit’s enrollment check passes.

Change an enrollment to see a parameterized check fail for just that program. Then inspect the expanded results and compare the shared residence checks.
